--- stdout
quill: render Duck Quill painting scripts, without a window.

USAGE
  quill render <script.json> [options]     paint the script, save the picture
  quill check <script.json> [--detail]     paint without saving: where everything
                                           went, and what looks like a mistake
                                           (--detail: every group and use, also
                                           the ones inside others; --animation
                                           and --frame choose the frame shown)
  quill export <script.json> [options]     an animated script as a sprite sheet
                                           with its JSON, frames, a GIF or an MP4
  quill info <picture.quill>               describe a saved picture: its layers
  quill info <script.json>                 the same for the picture a script
                                           paints, with the commands that
                                           painted on each layer
  quill measure "some text" [--size n]     how wide and high a text would be
                                           (and the size that fits --fit width)
  quill atlas <a.json> <b.json> ...        tiles or sprites (one script each)
                                           packed into one PNG with a JSON of
                                           where each one is, for a game
  quill presets                            the built-in brush presets, for
                                           {"cmd": "brush", "preset": "..."}
  quill views <script.json> [options]      the picture seven ways on one sheet
                                           (<name>-views.png): as painted, gray,
                                           squinted, a thumbnail, flipped, the
                                           named parts' silhouettes, and a heat
                                           map of where the eye goes, with the
                                           intent's focal point ringed
  quill critique <script.json> [options]   about fifteen findings in numbers:
                                           values, focal point, colour and key,
                                           texture, readability at thumbnail
                                           size, composition (warnings to look
                                           at, never goals)
  quill palette <picture> [--colors n]     the main colours of a PNG, JPEG or
                                           script, as swatches (<name>-palette.png)
                                           and a palette block to paste
  quill values <picture>                   the picture in five greys
                                           (<name>-values.png) with their shares
  quill compare <mine> <reference>         both side by side with their greys
                                           (compare.png), and how alike they are
                                           in value structure and colour, 0-100
  quill gallery add <script> --name <n>    a finished piece into the gallery:
                                           its folder with the picture, process
                                           and views sheets, critique.md, a
                                           blind-read skeleton, notes and an
                                           index entry with tags
  quill gallery rate <name> <1-5> "why"    the person's rating into index.json
  quill blind-read <script.json>           the leak-proof blind-read test: a packet
                                           (the picture under a neutral name and
                                           the three questions, nothing else) for
                                           a reader who wasn't told the intent;
                                           --record answers.txt --verdict "reads"
                                           writes blind-read.md next to the script
  quill --version                          the version number
  quill help                               show this
  quill <command> --help                   just that command's part of it

RENDER OPTIONS
  --out <folder>     where to save (default: out)
  --snapshots        also save a picture at every `snapshot` command and
                     whenever the script moves on from a layer it painted
  --sheet            save one image with all those pictures side by side
  --preview          paint smaller, for a quick look (longest side 800 px)
  --scale <s>        paint at this size, e.g. 0.5 for half (instead of --preview)
  --crop x,y,w,h     save only this part, at full size, to check details
                     (it may go past the edges: outside shows as grey squares)
  --zoom <n>         also save <name>-zoom<n>.png, n times bigger (pixels
                     become squares); <name>.png stays its own size. Crops,
                     previews and sheets are shown enlarged
  --transparent      leave the paper out of the PNG (see-through background)
  --layers "A,B"     show only these layers (the .quill keeps them all)
  --hide "A,B"       show all layers but these
  --bg <#RRGGBB>     with --transparent: this colour behind the see-through
                     parts of previews, crops, snapshots and sheets
  --grid <n>         a light grid every n canvas pixels, with coordinates,
                     on previews, crops and snapshots
  --detail           after rendering, list everything `check --detail` does
                     instead of the short summary
  --frame <n>        for a script with animations: paint frame n (from 0)
  --frames <a>-<b>   paint frames a to b; --all-frames paints every frame
  --animation <name> which animation, if the script has more than one
                     (frames are saved as <name>-<animation>-<frame>.png)
  --frame-sheet [n]  every frame (or every nth) in one picture, numbered,
                     as <name>-<animation>-frames.png
  --onion            with --frame n: the frame with the one before it faint
                     in red and the one after in blue, as ...-onion.png
  --pixels           for a pixel canvas: print the picture as rows of
                     letters, one per palette colour (. = see-through)
  --gif              every frame as <name>-<animation>.gif, for a quick look
  --tile             for a picture that repeats (a game background, a floor
                     tile): also <name>-tile.png, the picture 2 x 2, and a
                     warning where opposite edges don't meet

  Pictures for looking at (previews, crops, snapshots, sheets) get --bg and
  --grid; <name>.png and <name>.quill never do. At full size, the picture
  with them is saved as <name>-view.png.

VIEWS OPTIONS
  --out <folder>     where to save (default: out)
  --gray, --squint, --thumb, --flip, --silhouette, --heat
                     save that one view alone, as <name>-gray.png and so on
                     (any number of them; without any, the sheet is saved)
  --frame <n>        for a script with animations: frame n (from 0)
  --animation <name> which animation, if the script has more than one

PALETTE, VALUES AND COMPARE OPTIONS
  --out <folder>     where to save (default: out)
  --colors <n>       for palette: this many colours (default 8)

BLIND-READ OPTIONS
  --out <folder>     where the packet goes (default: out)
  --record <file>    the reader's answers, to write into blind-read.md
  --verdict "..."    with --record: "reads", or "doesn't read: why"

GALLERY OPTIONS
  --out <folder>     the gallery (default: skills/duck-quill/gallery)
  --title "..."      for add: the piece's title (default: the script's)
  --tags a,b         for add: tags besides the ones found in the intent and
                     the tools used

CRITIQUE OPTIONS
  --detail           also every named part's numbers (texture, thumbnail size)
  --score            also the benchmark's five scores from the numbers
  --frame <n>        for a script with animations: critique frame n (from 0)
  --frames <a>-<b>   one short line per frame, and which frame is worst
  --animation <name> which animation, if the script has more than one

EXPORT OPTIONS (for scripts with animations; docs/sprite-sheet-format.md)
  --out <folder>     where to save (default: out)
  --sheet            <name>.png (one row per animation) and <name>.json: the
                     default when nothing else is asked for
  --frames           every frame as <name>-<animation>-<frame>.png
  --gif              <name>-<animation>.gif, at the animation's fps
  --mp4              <name>-<animation>.mp4 through ffmpeg (or the frames and
                     the exact ffmpeg command to run, if it isn't installed)
  --scale <n>        n times bigger, with sharp pixels (for pixel art)
  --bg <#RRGGBB>     behind see-through parts of GIFs and MP4s (an MP4 uses
                     the paper colour if not given)
  --animation <name> only this animation

ATLAS OPTIONS (docs/sprite-sheet-format.md, "Tilesets")
  --out <folder>     where to save (default: out)
  --name <name>      <name>.png and <name>.json (default: atlas)
  --columns <n>      tiles per row (default: about a square)
  --padding <n>      see-through pixels between tiles (default 0)
  --scale <n>        n times bigger, with sharp pixels (for pixel art)

EXAMPLES
  quill render examples/sunset.json --preview --sheet
  quill render examples/sunset.json --out render --snapshots
  quill render examples/sunset.json --crop 700,450,200,150 --zoom 3 --grid 50
  quill render examples/sunset.json --preview --layers "Sky,Sun"
  quill export examples/duck-animated.json --gif --scale 2 --bg "#4080A0"
  quill atlas tiles/grass.json tiles/water.json tiles/sand.json --name ground
  quill views examples/sunset.json
  quill critique examples/sunset.json
  quill palette skills/duck-quill/references/coffee.png --colors 6
  quill compare out/study.png skills/duck-quill/references/coffee.png
  quill gallery add out/forest.json --name forest-at-dawn
  quill blind-read out/forest.json

The script format is described in docs/script-format.md.
--- stderr
--- exit code 0
